user_query: We're studying a mouse model of cancer and have called large structural variants — big deletions and duplications — from tumour whole-genome sequencing. I just need a quick read on which genes and regulatory regions these large events disrupt.
confidence: SILVER (Opus-authored) — pending mentor validation, not gold

most_severe.note: want per-gene / per-feature overlap for the SV, not a single collapsed consequence

summary.note: want which genes/features are hit, not a summary line

justification: Mouse (non-human) somatic structural variants, quick consequence read: identify which genes (symbol, canonical, biotype, exon/intron numbers, CCDS — available for mouse) and which regulatory features (regulatory build — mouse has one) the large deletions/duplications overlap, with NMD to flag likely loss-of-function and Phenotypes (MGI) for gene context. confidence: SILVER (Opus-authored) — pending mentor validation, not gold

sift.note: protein-based missense predictor — not applicable to non-coding regulatory variants

polyphen.note: protein-based missense predictor — not applicable to non-coding regulatory variants

most_severe.note: need full detail across overlapping regulatory features

summary.note: need detailed annotations, not a summary

justification: Human germline non-coding variants in regulatory regions, clinical interpretation: the regulatory build (+ cell_type) to identify overlapping promoters/enhancers/TF motifs, UTRAnnotator for 5'UTR effects and Enformer for predicted regulatory impact; CADD as a genome-wide deleteriousness score that (unlike SIFT/PolyPhen) also scores non-coding positions, and SpliceAI for variants near splice regions; ClinVar + gnomAD for known-variant clinical significance and population frequency; gene identifiers for the nearby disease genes. Missense predictors (SIFT/PolyPhen) are explicitly OFF — they require a protein consequence and do not apply to regulatory variants.
